messages.subject: Re: geom_crossbar with continuous x
parts:
Hi:

Convert x to a factor in the geom_crossbar() call and you'll be fine:

ggplot(d) +
geom_crossbar(aes(x = as.factor(x), y = y2, ymin = y1, ymax = y3)) +
xlab('x')

I can see where you got the impression from the 0.8.9 help pages that
x could be continuous, but as you discovered, when you try it, the
result is 'unexpected' :) For geom_crossbar(), geom_errorbar[h](),
geom_boxplot() and related geoms associated with distributions at
individual values of a variable x, it's safer to assume that x should
be a factor. If you need to connect aspects of the distributions with
lines, then use the group = aesthetic.

HTH,
Dennis

On Sun, Jun 17, 2012 at 10:14 PM, Mark Seeto <mark...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dear ggplot2 group,
>
> Can I do a geom_crossbar plot with a continuous x variable? The manual page
> for geom_crossbar says "continuous" is a related scale for x, which suggests
> it is possible, but I get an unexpected result.
>
> Example:
> d <- data.frame(x = c(1, 1.5, 3.2), y1 = c(0, 0.5, 0.7), y2 = c(1, 2,
> 2.5), y3 = c(2, 2.7, 4))
> ggplot(data=d) + geom_crossbar(aes(x=x, y = y2, ymin = y1, ymax = y3))
>
> I'm using ggplot version 0.9.0. Thanks for any help you can give.
>
> Mark

messages.author: ee65f9feb643484e
messages.subject: Re: geom_crossbar with continuous x
parts:
Thanks for your reply, Dennis. The problem with your solution is that
I want the x positions to be non-uniform, as indicated by the x
values.

Winston Chang gave me the following solution, which does what I want:
ggplot(data=d) + geom_crossbar(aes(x=x, y = y2, ymin = y1, ymax = y3,
group=x), fill="white")

Mark
